rules.title: SQL query built by string concatenation
rules.description: A SQL statement is assembled by concatenating a string literal with another expression. If any part of that expression reaches the request, an attacker controls the query's structure, not just its data.
rules.remediation: Use parameterized queries (placeholders bound by the driver). Never interpolate into SQL, including for identifiers - allowlist those instead.

rules.title: SQL query built with an f-string or .format()
rules.description: f-strings and .format() interpolate directly into the SQL text. The database receives whatever the user typed as query syntax.
rules.remediation: Pass parameters as the second argument: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = %s', (user_id,)).

rules.title: Django raw()/extra() with interpolated SQL
rules.description: Django's raw() and extra() do not escape interpolated values; only the params= argument is bound safely.
rules.remediation: Use Model.objects.raw('... WHERE id = %s', [value]) and pass values through params.

rules.title: Raw SQL helper called with a template literal
rules.description: A template literal with ${} inside a raw SQL helper interpolates before the driver sees it.
rules.remediation: Use bindings: knex.raw('select * from t where id = ?', [id]) or sequelize replacements.

rules.title: subprocess call with shell=True
rules.description: shell=True hands the argument to /bin/sh, so shell metacharacters in any interpolated value become commands.
rules.remediation: Pass a list of arguments and leave shell=False. If you need a pipeline, build it with subprocess pipes rather than a shell string.

rules.title: os.system() call
rules.description: os.system() always runs through a shell and returns only an exit code. Any interpolated value is shell syntax.

rules.title: child_process.exec with an interpolated command
rules.description: exec() spawns a shell. Template interpolation into it is command injection.
rules.remediation: Use execFile()/spawn() with an argument array, which never involves a shell.

rules.title: Shell interpolation in Ruby backticks or system()
rules.description: Ruby interpolates #{} before the shell runs the string.
rules.remediation: Use the multi-argument form: system('git', 'checkout', branch).

rules.title: PHP shell execution with a variable
rules.description: A PHP variable reaches a shell execution function.
rules.remediation: Avoid shell execution. If unavoidable, use escapeshellarg() on every interpolated value.

rules.title: eval()/exec() on a non-literal expression
rules.description: eval() and exec() execute arbitrary Python. Reaching them with request data is remote code execution.
rules.remediation: Use ast.literal_eval() for data, a dispatch dict for behaviour, or json.loads() for structured input.

rules.title: eval() or Function() constructor on dynamic input
rules.description: eval() and the Function constructor compile strings into code in the caller's scope.
rules.remediation: Parse data with JSON.parse(). For dynamic dispatch use an object map keyed by an allowlisted name.

rules.title: vm module used as a sandbox
rules.description: Node's vm module is not a security boundary - escaping it via constructor chains is a documented, trivial technique.
rules.remediation: Run untrusted code in a separate process with dropped privileges, or not at all.

rules.title: PHP eval() or dynamic include with a variable
rules.description: Dynamic include and eval turn a controllable string into executed PHP - the classic path to remote code execution and local file inclusion.
rules.remediation: Map user input to a fixed allowlist of file paths. Never eval.

rules.title: Template rendered from a string built at runtime
rules.description: Jinja2 evaluates the template source. A user-controlled template is server-side template injection, which reaches Python objects and therefore RCE.
rules.remediation: Render a fixed template file and pass user data as a context variable.

rules.title: MongoDB $where or JS evaluation clause
rules.description: $where evaluates JavaScript on the database server against every document.
rules.remediation: Express the condition with standard query operators. Disable server-side JS on the mongod.

rules.title: Request object passed straight into a query filter
rules.description: If the request body is used as a filter, a client can send {"$ne": null} where a string was expected and match every document - the standard NoSQL auth bypass.
rules.remediation: Cast and validate each field before it reaches the query: String(req.body.user).

rules.title: LDAP filter built by concatenation
rules.description: Unescaped input in an LDAP filter lets an attacker rewrite the filter, typically to *)(uid=* for an authentication bypass.
rules.remediation: Escape with the platform's LDAP filter encoder before interpolating.

rules.title: XPath expression built by concatenation
rules.description: Concatenated XPath allows the same class of logic rewriting as SQL injection.
rules.remediation: Use variable binding via XPathVariableResolver or an equivalent.

rules.title: Unsanitized input written to a log line
rules.description: Newlines in user input let an attacker inject fake log entries, which breaks log-based investigation.
rules.remediation: Log with structured fields rather than interpolation, and strip CR/LF from user-supplied values.
